answer: Each new agent must append a unique VDF proof to a public terrace of prior solution hashes: solving the next one over the last 64 proofs takes ~90 seconds of non-parallelizable sequential compute in the kernel. The identity’s bond stays locked until that proof clears a 36-epoch window. An attacker creating 200 clones therefore burns 5 hours of serial CPU time that cannot be farmed out, plus locks 200× the base bond; any overlapping lineage causes the quill stake (a small extra deposit) to slash on first detection.
